All 5 critical invariants verified:  (1) Deterministic layer is PRIMARY — CODEFORGE_LLM_MOD_DISABLED=1 → analyze_message_combined() still returns layer_local (layer='local', score reflects spam keywords) with layer_llm=None. critical_code_review_comments: bot_analyzer.analyze_message_combined() correctly enforces 2-layer independence: layer_local computed FIRST synchronously (deterministic score = keyword+flood+repeat+paste+mention_flood), then optional layer_llm as SECOND additive pass. combined_score = max(local, llm) — no averaging that could hide a signal.
_llm_analyze_subtle catches all exceptions, wraps errors in {layer:'llm', error:str} — never propagates upward. asyncio.wait_for(timeout=6.0) prevents blocking /groups/send indefinitely.
CODEFORGE_LLM_MOD_DISABLED env var read at call-time (not at import), so tests can toggle it per-test with no module reload. Verified across 18 new tests.

social_routes.py /groups/send correctly checks social_prefs.anonymous for sender BEFORE constructing notif doc; identity fields only added inside `if not sender_is_anonymous:` block — no leak possible via structural bug. Verified via runtime DB roundtrip.
mentions_routes._sanitize provides defense-in-depth: even if a legacy row had leaked identity fields stored, they are stripped on read when author_hidden=true.

mod_alerts doc structure: {alert_id, group_type, reasons[], score, layer_local, layer_llm, sender_key_id, message_ids, state, created_at, assigned_to?} — both layer_local and layer_llm keys ALWAYS present (verified by runtime insert + fetch).
GROUP_TYPES uses English keys ('private' not 'prive'); this is a minor style inconsistency with French UI but not a bug — front-end maps them.

Test isolation: initial invariants tests used asyncio.get_event_loop() which fails after prior tests close the loop — fixed by introducing _run_async() helper that creates fresh event loop per test. All 151 tests now run cleanly in the same session.

Anonymous-safe rule is enforced in TWO places (defense-in-depth): (a) social_routes.py never STORES identity when anonymous, (b) mentions_routes._sanitize() FILTERS identity on READ if author_hidden=true. Both were runtime-verified.
